arithmetic_conclusions.reason: Each purchase has at least one entry and rejects additions above uint128.max - totalEntries, so ticketCount <= totalEntries and all range endpoints fit.
Maximum gross sales use 148 bits; the largest percentage numerator uses 161 bits.
Every gross amount is a multiple of 1,000,000; each entry allocates exactly 50,000 protocol units and 800,000 cash-winner units.
The NFT branch assigns exactly 950,000 units per entry; the cash branch assigns exactly 150,000 units per entry.
Disjoint live ticket ranges sum to no more than totalEntries; duplicate IDs fail after the first burn, and any failure reverts the batch.
Modulo selects a value in [1,totalEntries], and totalEntries is positive in Drawing; unminted zero ranges cannot prove a positive winner.
The winning entry fits uint128 by construction; timestamp casts require times above 2**64 to truncate, outside realistic execution.
Requests and callbacks reject the exact deadline at which refunds become available; uint256 deadline additions cannot overflow from uint64 inputs.
Both fee checks reject underpayment and msg.value - paidPrice cannot underflow; a failed refund reverts the request.
Direct token donations do not affect tracked liabilities, entry counts, fees, or win probabilities.
At most one extra 256-bit random-word preimage reaches any entry; the relative difference stays below 2**-128 under the uint128 entry cap.
